title: Sliced Reserved Pools & Elastic Failover for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Marco Alvarez
summary: Introduce 'sliced' sub-reservations inside dedicated pools with elastic failover rules to let teams safely share reserved capacity while preserving isolation guarantees and predictable autoscaling behavior.
problem_statement: Large customers request more granular allocation inside reserved GPU pools: product teams want to carve predictable slices for business units while allowing controlled burst and automatic failover to non-reserved capacity during spikes. Today reserved pools are monolithic (tenant-level), leading to inefficient utilization, risky manual reallocation, and poor tenant isolation under contention.
goals: Allow admins to create lightweight 'slices' (sub-reservations) inside an existing reserved pool with quota and headroom settings
Provide autoscaling policies that grow/shrink a pool and its slices within enforced guardrails (min/max, predictive headroom)
Implement burst policies that differentiate soft (best-effort) and hard (contractual) capacity, enforcing tenant fencing to prevent noisy-neighbor degradation
Offer a deterministic elastic failover path to hosted/dedicated shared capacity with audit logs and rollback safeguards
Expose console UI and API to observe slice utilization, reservation health, and prewarming metrics
non_goals: Not expanding to full multi-cloud cross-region capacity pooling in this phase
Not changing core billing models — billing per existing reserved capacity units only
Not building tenant-level RBAC beyond slice ownership and admin controls (advanced RBAC later)
user_stories: As a Platform Admin, I can create a slice inside a reserved pool and set min/max units plus burst allowance
As a Team Owner, I can request additional temporary headroom from the pool via a transparent 'burst' request and see whether it was granted
As an SRE, I can configure an autoscale policy that expands the pool by N GPUs when 95th percentile utilization exceeds X for Y minutes
As a Product Engineer, I can opt my service into a soft-burst policy that will degrade gracefully before eviction of hard-reserved slices
As an Operator, I can trigger a controlled failover that moves selected traffic to a warm fallback model variant in hosted capacity and see audit trail
functional_requirements: API: POST /pools/{pool_id}/slices to create a slice with fields {name, owner, min_units, max_units, burst_policy_id}
API: PATCH /slices/{slice_id} to update min/max units and headroom constraints
Autoscaler: policy config objects supporting conditions (utilization, queue length, latency) and actions (+units, -units) with cooldowns
Burst policy types: soft_burst (best-effort), firm_burst (priority with preemption protection budget), emergency_burst (operator-approved)
Isolation: tenant fencing flags that prevent soft-burst consumers from evicting hard-reserved slices; enforced at scheduler/runtime
Failover: declarative route rules to send traffic to fallback targets (hosted, different zone, model-variant) when slice headroom is exhausted
Telemetry: per-slice metrics (token/sec, requests/sec, latency P50/P95/P99, kv-cache hits, prewarm status) exported to console and metrics backend
Auditing: record create/update/delete actions, autoscale events, burst grants/denials, and failovers with timestamps and initiator
nonfunctional_requirements: SLOs: autoscale decision latency < 30s from signal to reservation change in 95% cases
Performance: scheduling overhead for slicing must not increase median scheduling latency by more than 5%
Reliability: failover actions must have a rollback path and should succeed in > 99% of controlled dry-run tests
Security: any API that modifies slices requires admin role and mTLS between control plane and cluster control agents
Scalability: support 10k slices per cluster without linear degradation in scheduler performance
Observability: console must surface 7d and 30d utilization histograms and per-slice incident breadcrumbs
acceptance_criteria: Create slice: platform admin creates a slice via API and UI; slice appears in console with correct min/max and owner
Autoscale rule: configured autoscale policy triggers an increase in pool units during load test and reduces when load subsides; metrics show headroom changes
Burst enforcement: soft_burst requests are denied when tenant fencing prevents eviction and the denial is recorded in audit logs
Failover path: simulated pool exhaustion triggers the failover rule; traffic is routed to fallback target; telemetry records transition and rollback works
Isolation: a hard-reserved slice under sustained peak maintains its min_units and maintains latency SLO while other slices are throttled
Telemetry & Audit: all events (create/update/autoscale/burst/failover) are visible in console and exported to metrics/audit backends within 60s
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal alpha - implement APIs and runtime enforcement; enable feature flag in non-prod clusters; run integration tests
Phase 1: Beta customers - invite 3 enterprise customers to test slices in a single region; collect feedback and iterate; require signed NDA
Phase 2: Gradual rollout - enable for all dedicated customers behind opt-in; monitor metrics and SLOs; provide migration playbook
Phase 3: GA - enable UI in console, publish docs, and open API to all tenants; remove experimental flags after 3 successful weeks
metrics_success: Utilization increase: +8-12% effective pooled utilization across participating pools within 30 days
Headroom accuracy: predictive autoscaler achieves < 10% overshoot/undershoot on reserved units in 95% of scaling events
Customer satisfaction: beta customers report 'useful' or 'very useful' for slicing in > 80% responses
Incident reduction: reduce manual reallocation incidents for reserved pools by 75% in quarter after GA
dependencies: PM-712459 - dedicated preemptible credit pools (billing/credits policy)
Console-645 - new table components for per-slice views (frontend)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Misconfigured autoscaler could over-allocate GPUs causing cost spikes. Mitigation: introduce budget caps and dry-run mode with alerting before automatic actions.
Risk: New slice metadata increases scheduler complexity and slows allocation. Mitigation: add index and cache layer; benchmark at 10k slices.
Risk: Customers rely on soft-burst and expect hard guarantees. Mitigation: clear UI/contract language and SLA matrix; expose 'hard' vs 'soft' indicators in console.
Risk: Audit logs expose sensitive tenant identifiers. Mitigation: apply redaction policy and role-based access to audit trails.
open_questions: How should we charge for temporary burst headroom? bill against owner's reserved units or bill to pool owner?
What is the minimum useful unit for slice min_units (GPU fractionalization vs whole GPUs)?
Should slices be transferable between pools or require deletion/recreation?
Operator UX for emergency_burst approvals: modal in console vs API-driven approval flow?
notes: This PRD intentionally combines allocation-level controls (slices) with operational controls (autoscale & failover). We will iterate on billing and RBAC after initial beta. Coordinate closely with legal on audit exposure and with SRE for safe canarying.
